To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
strawberries can be acceptably considered to be spheres, and that a new correlation for determining surface heat transfer coefficient of strawberries is proposed.
the heat transfer coefficients of the air cooling process of strawberries are higher than those predicted for spheres by the correlation of the McAdams.

1) the effective surface heat transfer coefficients for air-cooled strawberries were 16-25% higher than the coefficients for spheres cooled only through convection, and 2) for air-cooled strawberry, a geometry correction for shape anomaly does not cause significant difference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mathematical model to describe the cooling rate of strawberries in air.

the development of a new method for determining effective surface heat transfer coefficients during air cooling of strawberries, which includes the effect on the surface heat transfer coefficient due to moisture evaporation.
the development of an analytical model that can be used to determine the surface heat transfer coefficients of a spherical fruit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation proposed for strawberries is a useful tool for predicting the heat transfer coefficients in forced convection cooling of strawberries.
the correlation developed in this study is valid to predict heat transfer coefficients for air precooling strawberry fruits.
the heat transfer coefficient for the cooling of strawberries in air is a function of Reynolds number and moisture evaporation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface heat transfer coefficients for strawberries are higher than for spheres and that they can be determined by the use of a correlation which takes into account the effect of moisture loss.
the heat transfer coefficient of the strawberries was 25% greater than the heat transfer coefficient for a sphere.
the heat transfer coefficient for strawberries is a function of air velocity and the strawberry moisture evaporation rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat transfer coefficient is not only a function of temperature difference, but also of the evaporation of water.
the use of a sphere as a reference geometry to predict heat transfer coefficients of fruits is acceptable.
the use of a single value for the surface heat transfer coefficient for the cooling of strawberries is not recommended.
